plan.name: The 20-Week Integrated Strength Program (V26.9: Longevity Update)
plan.description: Build elite pulling strength (max pull-ups, pull-up variations) while maintaining all-around capacity (pushing, lower body) and protecting knee/shoulder health. Optimized for the 40+ athlete with Volume Management and Joint Longevity principles.
plan.author: V26.9 Program

triggers: Sharp pain during Ring Rows or PPPU
Shoulder pinch or impingement on Dips or HSPU

coldStartRowerProtocol.protocol: Min 1-2: Zone 1, Min 3-4: Zone 2, Min 5: 3x10s Sprints

straightArmPulldownProgression.description: Lat and scapular activation on Day 1 & Day 5 warm-ups
straightArmPulldownProgression.cycle: 4-week progression (W1: 3x12 RPE6, W2: 3x15 RPE6-7, W3: 4x12 RPE7, W4: Deload 2-3x12 RPE5-6)
straightArmPulldownProgression.notes: Stop before elbow irritation; substitute with chest-supported rows if needed

rtoRingSupportHolds.description: Moderate RTO ring support holds for shoulder stability
rtoRingSupportHolds.notes: Integrated into existing Ring Support Hold exercises; switch to parallel holds if anterior pinch occurs

repBeforeLoadRule.description: Double Progression: Add weight only when hitting top rep range for all sets with perfect form

programRules.dipGovernorRule: If shoulder pinch occurs during weighted dips, switch to Straight Bar Dips or Weighted Bench Dips
programRules.gripSaverProtocol: Day 5 core work must be ground-based (V-Ups/Hollows) to prevent medial epicondylitis

day4CoreWork.description: Day 4 active recovery with core training. Focuses on anti-rotation, anti-extension, and rotational strength to complement the pulling and pushing days.

day4ElbowRehab.description: Optional elbow rehab routine can be added after core work if needed.
day4ElbowRehab.painGuidelines: Traffic light: 0-3 OK, 4-5 acceptable (do not progress), >5 back off. 24-hour rule: if worse next morning, reduce load/volume ~50%.

neutralGripTracking.rule: Use the exact same neutral grip implement (rings, parallel bars, etc.) for the entire block

routineTemplates.name: Rower Protocol
routineTemplates.description: Cold Start Protocol before Day 1 & 5

routineTemplates.name: Assault Bike Protocol
routineTemplates.description: Cold Start Protocol before Day 1 & 5 - Assault Bike variant with power output technique focus

exercises.notes: Min 1-2: Easy pace. TECHNIQUE FOCUS: Full push-pull coordination - drive handles forward as legs extend, pull back as legs recover. Smooth circular motion.
cues: Push with legs, pull with arms
Breathe rhythmically - in for 2, out for 2

exercises.notes: Min 3-4: Moderate pace. SKILL CHALLENGE: Practice 'power circles' - emphasize the push phase (legs + arms working together) rather than grinding. Find your sustainable rhythm.
cues: Power through the bottom of pedal stroke

exercises.notes: Min 5: 3 x 10s Max Effort Sprints. POWER FOCUS: Explosive start, aggressive arm pull, drive through heels. Each sprint is CNS priming - wake up fast-twitch fibers!
cues: Sprint 1: Practice explosive start from zero
Sprint 2: Focus on arm drive intensity

routineTemplates.name: Jump Rope Protocol
routineTemplates.description: Cold Start Protocol before Day 1 & 5 - Jump Rope variant with rhythm and coordination progression

exercises.notes: Min 1-2: Single unders, relaxed rhythm. TECHNIQUE FOCUS: Minimize vertical jump height - think 'hover' not 'bounce'. Wrists do the work, arms stay still. Land softly on balls of feet.
cues: Rotate rope from wrists, not shoulders
Stay on the balls of your feet

exercises.notes: Min 3-4: Steady pace, maintain form. SKILL CHALLENGE: Try alternating foot singles (boxer skip) for 10-15 seconds, then back to regular bounce. This teaches weight transfer and coordination.
cues: Challenge: Can you do 20 unbroken jumps?

exercises.notes: Min 5: 3 x 10s Fast singles or double unders. POWER CHALLENGE: If you can do double unders, go for it! If not, fast singles with wrist snap intensity. This is about speed and rhythm, not perfection.
cues: Sprint 1: Fast singles - quick wrist turnover
Sprint 2: Attempt 1-2 double unders OR faster singles
Sprint 3: All-out speed - push your rope speed limit!

routineTemplates.name: Burpees Protocol
routineTemplates.description: Cold Start Protocol before Day 1 & 5 - Burpees variant (no equipment) with movement quality focus

exercises.notes: Min 1-2: Controlled pace, focus on form. TECHNIQUE FOCUS: Perfect each phase - hinge to hands, step or jump back to plank (hollow body!), chest to floor, push up, step/jump feet to hands, stand tall. Quality over speed.
cues: Phase breakdown: Squat → Plank → Push-up → Jump in → Stand
Keep core braced in plank position
Full chest to floor on each rep

exercises.notes: Min 3-4: Increase pace slightly. SKILL CHALLENGE: Practice the 'flow state' - smooth transitions between phases. Can you make it look effortless? Breathing rhythm: exhale on push-up, inhale on jump-in.
cues: Breathe: exhale pushing up, inhale standing

exercises.notes: Min 5: 3 x 10s Max effort burpees. EXPLOSIVE POWER: Sprint pace! Jump back aggressively, explosive push-up, power jump to hands, explosive stand. CNS activation - move FAST but maintain form.
cues: Sprint 3: All-out speed - count your reps!

routineTemplates.name: Mountain Climbers Protocol
routineTemplates.description: Cold Start Protocol before Day 1 & 5 - Mountain Climbers variant (no equipment) with core control emphasis

exercises.notes: Min 1-2: Slow controlled pace, knees to chest. TECHNIQUE FOCUS: Perfect plank position first! Hands under shoulders, neutral spine, hips level. Drive knee toward same-side elbow, fully extend back. No hip bobbing!
cues: Start in strong plank - hollow body
Hips stay level - don't bounce up and down
Drive knee to elbow, not just forward

exercises.notes: Min 3-4: Moderate pace, maintain plank position. SKILL CHALLENGE: Focus on 'running in place' rhythm. Can you maintain perfect plank for the full 2 minutes? Core anti-rotation challenge - resist twisting!
cues: Run in place - alternate legs rhythmically

exercises.notes: Min 5: 3 x 10s Max speed sprints. POWER OUTPUT: Sprint your legs as fast as possible while maintaining plank integrity! This is CNS activation - explosive hip flexor action meets core stability.
cues: Sprint 1: Fast leg drive - count reps per side
Sprint 2: Even faster - can you beat sprint 1?
Sprint 3: All-out leg speed while keeping shoulders still!

routineTemplates.name: Day 4 Core Routine
routineTemplates.description: Active recovery core work focusing on anti-rotation, anti-extension, and rotational strength. Complements pulling and pushing days while maintaining joint health.

exercises.notes: Anti-extension core work. HOW TO: (1) Lie on back with arms extended toward ceiling, knees bent 90°. (2) Press lower back flat into floor. (3) Slowly extend opposite arm and leg, maintaining lower back contact with floor. (4) Return to start and switch sides. Focus on breathing and control.
cues: Lower back stays glued to floor throughout

exercises.notes: Anti-rotation core stability. HOW TO: (1) Attach band to anchor point at chest height. (2) Stand perpendicular to anchor, band in both hands at chest. (3) Press hands straight out, resisting rotation. (4) Hold 2 seconds, return to chest. (5) Complete all reps one side, then switch.
cues: Press straight out (don't let band pull you)

exercises.notes: Adductor and lateral core strength. HOW TO: (1) Set up in side plank position with top leg elevated on bench/box at knee height. (2) Bottom leg hangs freely or rests lightly on ground. (3) Hold side plank position, engaging top adductor to keep leg elevated. (4) Maintain straight line from head to heels.
exercises.progressionNotes: Start with bottom leg on ground for support. Progress to bottom leg elevated off ground. Advanced: add hip abduction pulses.
cues: Top leg actively pushes into bench

exercises.notes: Core compression and anti-extension. HOW TO: (1) Lie on back, arms extended overhead. (2) Press lower back into floor. (3) Lift shoulders and legs slightly off ground. (4) Hold position, maintaining lower back contact with floor.
exercises.progressionNotes: Start with knees bent if needed. Progress to straight legs, then arms overhead.

exercises.notes: Anti-rotation and anti-extension from quadruped. HOW TO: (1) Start on hands and knees, spine neutral. (2) Slowly extend opposite arm and leg, keeping hips level. (3) Hold 2 seconds at full extension. (4) Return with control and switch sides.

Rotational core strength. HOW TO: (1) Sit with knees bent, feet elevated slightly off ground. (2) Lean back ~45°, maintaining neutral spine. (3) Hold weight at chest, rotate torso side to side, tapping weight to floor beside hips. (4) Focus on rotating through thoracic spine, not just moving arms.
exercises.progressionNotes: Start with bodyweight or light plate. Progress load only when form is perfect.
cues: Rotate from ribcage, not just arms
Feet stay off ground (or modify with heels down)

exercises.notes: Anti-rotation plank variation. HOW TO: (1) Start in high plank position. (2) Tap one hand to opposite shoulder while minimizing hip rotation. (3) Alternate sides. (4) Keep hips level and core braced throughout.

routineTemplates.name: Day 4 Elbow Rehab (Optional)
routineTemplates.description: Optional rehab session for lateral/medial elbow tendinopathy. Use Traffic Light: 0-3 OK, 4-5 acceptable, >5 reduce. 24-hour rule: if worse next morning, cut load/volume by ~50%.

exercises.notes: Aim ~70% effort (strong contraction, no shaking). HOW TO: (1) Sit/stand tall with shoulders relaxed. (2) Bend elbow ~90° and support forearm on thigh/bench so only wrist can move (hand hangs off edge). (3) Set wrist in slight extension (lateral) or slight flexion (medial). (4) Apply resistance with a light DB or your other hand and hold absolutely still for 45s. Pain during holds should stay ≤5/10 and ideally feel better (or neutral) afterward.
exercises.progressionNotes: Progress by adding 5-10s per hold (up to 60s), then increase resistance slightly. If next-day pain/stiffness increases, reduce total volume ~50%.
cues: Support forearm; hand hangs off edge
Wrist neutral → slight extension/flexion depending on option
Match resistance to symptoms: firm effort, no shaking
Grip only as hard as needed; don't crank fingers

exerciseOptions.description: For lateral elbow pain (tennis elbow). Palm down; hold wrist slightly extended and resist extension.
For medial elbow pain (golfer's elbow). Palm up; hold wrist slightly flexed and resist flexion.

exercises.notes: Slow 4s eccentric. Use a very light DB. HOW TO: (1) Support forearm on bench/thigh with wrist hanging off edge. (2) Use the non-working hand to lift the DB to the top position (concentric assist). (3) Release the assist and LOWER with the working wrist only for a full 4 seconds. (4) At the bottom, re-grip with the assist hand and reset for the next rep. This should feel hard in the tendon/muscle, not sharp in the joint.
exercises.progressionNotes: Add load last. First: reduce symptoms and nail tempo. Then add 1-2 reps/set (up to 20) or add a small load increment.
cues: Forearm supported on bench/box, wrist over edge
No swinging; keep the movement isolated at the wrist
Use the other hand to lift; ONLY the lowering is 'work'

exerciseOptions.description: Palm down. Start in extension (hand up), lower toward flexion over 4 seconds.
Palm up. Start in flexion (hand up), lower toward extension over 4 seconds.

exercises.notes: Tempo 3s up / 3s down. HOW TO: (1) Sit with forearm supported on bench/thigh, palm down, wrist hanging off edge. (2) Start with wrist slightly flexed. (3) Curl wrist up into extension over 3 seconds. (4) Lower back down over 3 seconds. Keep the movement at the wrist only. Choose a load that stays smooth and controlled. Pain ≤5/10.
exercises.progressionNotes: HSR progression: W1-2: 3x15, W3-4: 3x12, W5-6: 3x10, W7-8: 4x8, W9-12: 4x6 (only if pain/stiffness trends down).
cues: Full ROM without snapping into end range

exercises.notes: Tempo 3s up / 3s down. HOW TO: (1) Sit with forearm supported, palm up, wrist hanging off edge. (2) Start with wrist slightly extended. (3) Curl wrist up into flexion over 3 seconds. (4) Lower back down over 3 seconds. Keep fingers relaxed (don't death-grip the DB). If this irritates lateral elbow, reduce range, reduce load, or skip for now.
exercises.progressionNotes: Progress only if next-day symptoms are stable or improving. If medial elbow is primary issue, prioritize this over extension work.

exercises.notes: Slow controlled rotations; hold end range 1s. HOW TO: (1) Hold a hammer by the handle (or a DB by one end to create a lever). (2) Elbow at ~90° and pinned to ribs, forearm parallel to floor. (3) Rotate slowly palm-up (supination) and pause 1s. (4) Rotate slowly palm-down (pronation) and pause 1s. Keep wrist neutral and avoid shoulder rotation.
exercises.progressionNotes: Increase lever length (hold farther from head) before adding load. Keep elbow tucked to side.

exercises.notes: Gentle stretch; no aggressive pain. HOW TO: (1) Arm straight in front, palm down. (2) With the other hand, bend wrist down and curl fingers toward forearm. (3) Keep shoulder down and elbow straight. (4) Hold a mild stretch 30s and breathe.
cues: Ease off if you get nerve symptoms

exercises.notes: Gentle stretch; keep elbow straight. HOW TO: (1) Arm straight in front, palm up. (2) With the other hand, bend wrist back into extension and gently straighten fingers. (3) Keep shoulder down and elbow straight. (4) Hold a mild stretch 30s and breathe.

routineTemplates.name: Day 5 Warm-Up (Pull Intensity + Push)
routineTemplates.description: Complete Day 5 warm-up sequence: Cold Start Rower (5min) → Global Tendon Prep (5min) → Straight-Arm Band Pulldowns (3min) → Mobility & activation (spine, wrists, push prep). Total: ~15 minutes.
routineTemplates.notes: Day 5 Protocol: (1) Cold Start Rower (5min): Zone 1-2 with sprints. (2) Global Tendon Prep (5min): Band pull-aparts, external rotations, scapular pulls. (3) Straight-Arm Band Pulldowns (3min): 4-week progression cycle. (4) Mobility: Cat-Cow, T-spine rotations, wrist rocks. (5) Push Prep: Push-up plus.

exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Start from dead hang with arms fully extended and shoulders engaged (don't let shoulders collapse into ears). Pull chin over bar using lat activation, not just arms. Squeeze shoulder blades together at top. Lower with control for 2-3 seconds, maintaining shoulder engagement throughout. Avoid kipping or swinging - this is strict pull-ups only.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Ladders: 1, 2, 3 reps. Focus on perfect form.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Ladder protocol: Set 1 = 1 rep, Set 2 = 2 reps, Set 3 = 3 reps, Set 4 = 1 rep (repeats pattern). This allows volume accumulation without going to failure. Rest 120 seconds between all sets. Each rep should be perfect quality - if form breaks down, stop the set. This is volume work, not intensity work. Save energy for later weeks.
exerciseTemplates.progressionNotes: Volume accumulation phase. Do not fail sets.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Double Progression Rule applies
exerciseTemplates.progressionNotes: Earn weight increase only when hitting top rep range for ALL sets with perfect form
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Use dip belt or weighted vest. Start with small increments (2.5kg). Maintain the same form as bodyweight pull-ups - no shortening ROM or using momentum. The added weight should force stricter form, not compromise it. Focus on controlled eccentric (lowering) phase - this is where you build the most strength. Rest the full 120 seconds between sets.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Tempo 2-1-1-0. Stop if sharp pain
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Set rings at appropriate height - the more horizontal your body, the harder it is. Keep body in straight plank position throughout - no sagging hips or piking. Pull chest to rings, not just hands to chest. Squeeze shoulder blades together at top and pause for 1 second. Lower for 2 seconds with control. If you feel elbow pain, stop immediately - this is an early warning exercise.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Tempo 2-1-1-0
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Place hands on elevated surface (bench, box, or bar set at appropriate height). Body should form straight line from head to heels - don't let hips sag or pike up. Lower for 2 seconds until chest nearly touches surface, pause 1 second, press up for 1 second, no pause at top. Keep elbows at 45° angle to body. The elevation makes this easier than floor push-ups while maintaining perfect form. Lower the surface height as you get stronger.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Ground-Based. Watch for elbow tightness
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Lie on back, press lower back into ground. Lift shoulders and legs slightly off ground, arms extended overhead. Rock back and forth using core contraction - not momentum. Keep lower back pressed down throughout. If your back arches, your core isn't strong enough yet - reduce the range or hold static hollow position instead. This is ground-based to avoid grip strain and protect elbows.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Dip Governor Rule: If shoulder pinch occurs, switch immediately
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Start at top with arms locked, shoulders pulled down away from ears. Lower until upper arms are parallel to ground (90° elbow bend) or slightly below if comfortable. Keep elbows at 45° angle to body - don't let them flare wide. Push back up, maintaining shoulder depression. If you feel any shoulder pinch or impingement, stop immediately and switch to the alternative (bench dips or push-ups). This is the Dip Governor Rule in action.

exerciseTemplates.notes: EMOM Min 1: Left Leg
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Place left foot forward, right foot elevated behind on bench (laces down). Position front foot far enough forward so shin stays vertical at bottom. Hold dumbbells at sides. Lower under control until rear knee nearly touches ground. Keep torso upright - don't lean forward. Drive through front heel to stand. Front knee should track over toes, not caving inward. This is minute 1 of the EMOM superset.

exerciseTemplates.notes: EMOM Min 2: Right Leg
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Place right foot forward, left foot elevated behind on bench (laces down). Position front foot far enough forward so shin stays vertical at bottom. Hold dumbbells at sides. Lower under control until rear knee nearly touches ground. Keep torso upright - don't lean forward. Drive through front heel to stand. Front knee should track over toes, not caving inward. This is minute 2 of the EMOM superset.

exerciseTemplates.notes: EMOM Min 3. Arms straight overhead. If lower back arches, drop weight immediately
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Lie on back holding light plate or dumbbell overhead with straight arms. Press lower back into ground, lift shoulders and legs off ground into hollow body position. The weight increases difficulty exponentially. If your lower back arches even slightly, you're going too heavy - drop the weight immediately. Start with just 1.25-2.5kg. Rock gently while maintaining hollow position. This is minute 3 of the EMOM superset. Stop set if form breaks.
exerciseTemplates.progressionNotes: Start 1.25kg or 2.5kg. Progress to 5kg only when holding perfect form for 45s

exerciseTemplates.notes: Posterior chain focus
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Romanian Deadlift: Start standing with barbell at hips, slight knee bend. Push hips back while maintaining neutral spine - think about closing a car door with your butt. Lower bar down front of legs, keeping it close to body. Feel stretch in hamstrings. Bar should reach mid-shin to just below knee depending on flexibility. Return by driving hips forward and squeezing glutes. Keep shoulders back and chest proud throughout. This is NOT a squat - knees stay mostly locked.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Tempo 2-1-1-0. Squeeze glutes hard at top. Place weight on hip crease
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Lie on back with knees bent, feet flat on ground. Place barbell or plate across hip crease (use pad if needed). Lower for 2 seconds, pause 1 second with glutes touching ground (not resting), drive up for 1 second by squeezing glutes - NOT by extending lower back. At top, pelvis should be neutral - avoid hyperextending lumbar spine. Squeeze glutes maximally at top and pause. This is glute activation, not a lower back exercise.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Reinforce healthy squat patterns. Ankle mobility focus
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Hold dumbbell or kettlebell vertically at chest, elbows pointing down. Feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly out. Squat down while keeping chest up and weight at chest. The weight will naturally keep you upright. Go as deep as mobility allows while maintaining neutral spine. Drive through full foot to stand. This is THE squat to teach proper mechanics. If you can't go deep, work on ankle mobility.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Heels elevated. Knee-friendly squat pattern. Tempo 2-1-1-0
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Place heels on small plates or wedge (1-2 inches elevation). This shifts load to quads and allows deeper squat with less ankle mobility. Can be done with dumbbells at sides or goblet style. Lower for 2 seconds, pause 1 second at bottom, drive up for 1 second. This variation is incredibly knee-friendly despite going deep - the heel elevation reduces knee stress. Perfect for those with ankle mobility limitations.

exerciseOptions.notes: Focus on depth and control. Keep chest up.

exerciseOptions.description: Easier on back, good for mobility work
exerciseOptions.notes: Hold weight close to chest. Focus on upright torso.

exerciseOptions.description: Unilateral focus, improves balance and addresses imbalances
exerciseOptions.notes: Rear foot elevated. Control the descent. Each side separately.

exerciseOptions.description: No equipment needed, focus on endurance and form
exerciseOptions.notes: Perfect for travel or home workouts. Focus on tempo.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Tempo 2-1-1-0
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Attach band to sturdy anchor at face height. Grab ends with both hands, step back to create tension. Pull band toward face, separating hands as they approach (like making double bicep pose). Focus on pulling elbows back and squeezing shoulder blades together. Think 'pull apart' not just 'pull back'. Externally rotate shoulders at end position. Pause 1 second, then return with control over 2 seconds. This exercise is crucial for shoulder health and rear delt development.

Attach band to anchor at chest height. Stand perpendicular to anchor, hold band with both hands at chest. Brace core and press hands straight out in front of you, fully extending arms. The band will try to rotate your torso - resist this with your core. Hold extended position for 1-2 seconds, then return to chest. Keep hips and shoulders square throughout - no rotation. This is anti-rotation core training. Do all reps on one side, then switch to other side.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Shoulder Balance
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Attach band at elbow height. Stand sideways to anchor, arm closest to anchor bent 90° with elbow tucked to side. Grab band with that hand. Rotate forearm inward (toward belly) while keeping elbow pinned to side. Control the return. This targets the subscapularis and helps balance out all the external rotation from pulling exercises. Critical for shoulder health in pull-heavy programs.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Controlled rotation, no collapse of front knee
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Sit on floor with one leg in front bent 90°, other leg to side also bent 90°. Both knees and both feet should touch ground. Rotate entire body to switch leg positions - what was in front goes to side, what was on side comes to front. Move with control, don't let front knee collapse inward. If you can't get both knees down, that's your hip mobility baseline - work within your range. This exercise directly addresses hip internal and external rotation.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Slow controlled articular rotations; hold balance or use support
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Stand on one leg (use wall for balance if needed). Lift other knee up and out to side, creating largest circle possible with your hip joint. Move SLOWLY with control - this isn't about speed or momentum. Complete full circle in one direction, then reverse. You're exploring and expanding your hip's full range of motion. If you find sticky spots or limitations, that's valuable information about your hip mobility.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Thoracic rotation; knees stacked
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Lie on side with knees bent and stacked, arms extended in front. Keep bottom arm on ground and knees stacked throughout. Rotate top arm up and over, trying to touch ground behind you. Follow your hand with your eyes. This mobilizes thoracic spine rotation - critical for shoulder health and pulling mechanics. Don't force the rotation; breathe into the stretch and let mobility improve over time.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Knee-down option allowed
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Lie on side, prop up on elbow with forearm flat. Stack feet or stagger them. Lift hips off ground until body forms straight line. Hold this position while breathing normally. If full side plank is too hard, drop bottom knee to ground (half side plank). Focus on maintaining straight line from shoulder to knee/feet - don't let hips sag. This is anti-lateral flexion core training.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Knee-down variation
Mid-range position; focus on tendon stiffness
Slow, controlled; stay in shallow range
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Start with feet wider than shoulder-width. Shift weight to one leg, bending that knee while keeping other leg straight. Descend only to comfortable depth (shallow range) - don't force deep squat. Straight leg stays flat on ground with toes pointed up. Keep chest up and weight in heel of bent leg. This develops lateral hip mobility and single-leg strength. Progress depth gradually over weeks.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Low-tension option
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Lie on back with lower back pressed into ground. Lift legs with knees bent 90°, arms extended straight up. Slowly lower one leg until heel nearly touches ground while opposite arm reaches overhead. Return and repeat other side. exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Start on parallettes or low bars. Lean forward with straight arms, protract (push) shoulder blades forward, and lift knees to chest. Your weight should be balanced on your hands with feet off ground. This is an advanced skill requiring significant shoulder and core strength. Scapular protraction is key - don't let shoulder blades pinch together. Start with very short holds (6-8 seconds) and gradually increase. This builds toward full planche.

exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Add weight using dip belt or weight vest. Same technique as bodyweight dips but with added load. Start with small increments (2.5kg). The weight should force even stricter form. Lower until upper arms parallel to ground, keep elbows at 45°. If you feel any shoulder impingement with added weight, immediately drop the weight or switch to alternative. Double Progression: master the reps before adding weight.

exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Lie on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand. Keep elbows tucked at 30-45° angle to torso (close grip position). Lower dumbbells to mid-chest level with controlled eccentric. Press up and slightly inward without locking elbows. Maintain shoulder blades retracted and depressed throughout. Focus on tricep and inner chest engagement. Double Progression: master the reps before adding weight.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Substituted for Sliders. Heels on rower seat, lift hips, slide away and back
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Lie on back next to rower with heels on seat. Push seat away so legs are extended and lift hips off ground into bridge position. Keep hips elevated and use hamstrings to curl (pull) the seat toward you by bending knees. Extend legs back out while maintaining hip height. This is excellent hamstring isolation using the rower's sliding seat. Keep glutes engaged throughout to protect lower back.

exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Cluster training technique: Perform 3 reps, rest 15-20 seconds while hanging, then 3 more reps, rest 15-20s, then final 3 reps. This is ONE set. Take full 120s rest between cluster sets. The brief intra-set rests allow you to maintain higher quality reps throughout the set by clearing lactate without fully releasing the bar.
